title: Obsidian Vault Architectures
summary: Japanese Edition https://daisuke.masuda.tokyo/article-2026-10-26-0519 This slide deck is a technical reference that compares approaches to Obsidian vault design, centered on Ideaverse, PARA, kepano, and Zettelkasten, while also covering LifeOS, Bramses, JG Method, CyanVoxel, Starter Templates, and Shimmering Obsidian. It distinguishes between methodologies, public vaults, and operational layers, organizing them through the lenses of folders versus links, knowledge development versus action management, and minimal versus structured setups. It also presents applications for technical research, writing, and project management, along with a Hybrid Vault proposal that combines PARA’s activity-based classification with Ideaverse’s MOCs. Rather than claiming a single best solution, it recommends starting simple and expanding gradually according to retrieval paths, daily workflows, and the level of configuration one can realistically maintain.
ja_summary:
Obsidianの主要な設計手法（PARA、Zettelkasten等）を整理・比較した技術資料。

title: Surviving WAF Bypass: Building Stronger Authentication Defenses for WordPress Websites
summary:
Securing a WordPress website requires much more than installing a security plugin or configuring a Web Application Firewall (WAF). Even with a WAF in place, attackers can bypass security controls and exploit weaknesses in authentication, server configuration, and website administration.

These slides, presented at WordCamp Sofia 2026 on October 24, explore practical techniques and lessons learned from securing WordPress websites. The presentation focuses on building a multilayered security strategy that reduces vulnerabilities and strengthens protection against unauthorized access.

Topics covered include:

+ Hardening WordPress installations and applying security updates.

+ Securing file and directory ownership and permissions.

+ Isolating WordPress websites and their databases.

+ Reducing unnecessary plugins, themes, and exposed services.

+ Strengthening authentication with two-factor authentication (2FA).

+ Configuring firewalls and restricting administrative access.

+ Avoiding unnecessary FTP credentials and using secure server access.

+ Migrating and recovering WordPress installations without carrying over potential backdoors.

+ Use PressGate, a free WordPress plugin, to strengthen login.

PressGate provides an additional layer of security with TOTP-based authentication, IP blocking, login monitoring, behavior detection, and role-specific security policies. You can install it for free. More info at https://zindrex.com/pressgate

The central message: WordPress security is an ongoing operational discipline, not a one-time configuration. A WAF is an important defense, but effective protection requires multiple complementary security layers. These slides offer practical recommendations for WordPress developers, website administrators, and security professionals looking to build more resilient WordPress websites.

PressGate: https://zindrex.com/pressgate
Blog Post: https://lifemichael.com/en/sharing-my-experience-at-wordcamp-sofia-2026/

title: OLAP Database Systems: Architecture, Engineering & Operations
summary:
OLAP database systems explained from first principles to production: why columnar storage wins on analytical workloads, how OLAP engines are architected, and what it takes to engineer and operate them at scale.

A 65-slide executive technical briefing by Shiv Iyer, Founder and CEO of ChistaDATA Inc. and MinervaDB Inc., for CTOs, data platform leaders, data architects and senior engineers who are choosing, building or running an analytical database.

What the deck covers

S1. Why OLAP is different: OLTP vs OLAP workloads, anatomy of an analytic query, why row stores struggle with scans, thirty years of columnar database history, and today's OLAP landscape (ClickHouse, Apache Druid, Apache Pinot, StarRocks, Snowflake, Google BigQuery, Amazon Redshift, Databricks SQL, Trino with Iceberg, DuckDB).

S2. Columnar storage fundamentals: row vs column layout, I/O arithmetic, dictionary, RLE and delta encoding, LZ4, ZSTD, DoubleDelta and Gorilla codecs, vectorized execution and SIMD, late materialization (PREWHERE), sparse primary indexes, granules, data skipping, and why ORDER BY is the real index in a column store.

S3. OLAP architecture: a five-layer reference architecture, immutable parts and background merges, shared-nothing MPP vs separated storage and compute, distributed query execution, sharding keys and hot shards, replication and consensus with ClickHouse Keeper (Raft), materialized views and projections, joins in OLAP, and the lakehouse with open table formats (Apache Iceberg, Delta Lake).

S4. Engineering: data modelling (wide tables, star schema, dictionaries), sort key design, partitioning for lifecycle, data types and codecs, ingestion from batch files, Kafka and CDC with Debezium, insert batching and the TOO_MANY_PARTS trap, updates and deletes, query optimisation with EXPLAIN, anti-patterns, and honest benchmarking with p95/p99 latency.

S5. Operations: golden signals from system tables, HA and DR topology with RPO/RTO targets, capacity planning and SLOs, ClickHouse LTS upgrades (26.3 to 26.8), cost governance and FinOps, an incident severity model, and an OLAP operational maturity model.

Close: five habits that separate fast analytics platforms from expensive ones, and a 90-day plan from assessment to an operated platform.

Worked examples use ClickHouse 26.8 LTS. The concepts apply to columnar OLAP engines and cloud data warehouses generally. Teaching figures are labelled illustrative in the deck.

ChistaDATA (ClickHouse consulting, support and managed services): chistadata.com
MinervaDB (vendor-neutral database infrastructure): minervadb.com
ja_summary:
・分析用DB（OLAP）の仕組みやカラムナストレージの利点を、設計から運用まで体系的に解説する技術資料。
・ClickHouse等の具体例を通じ、大規模データ処理のアーキテクチャ、クエリ最適化、障害対応のベストプラクティスを網羅。
・CTOやデータアーキテクト向けに、分析基盤の構築・運用を最適化し、コストとパフォーマンスを両立させる指針を提示。
